newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Pilot in Brazil air crash veered to save school.
newsitem.headline: Pilot in Brazil air crash veered to save school.

text.p: One of the last actions of the pilot of a Fokker-100 plane that crashed on Thursday into a suburb of Sao Paulo was to avoid hitting a school packed with children, local Globo newspaper said on Saturday.
According to information on the plane's black box, or flight data recorder, pilot Jose Antonio Moreno told Congonhas airport control tower shortly after takeoff that he was returning, Globo said.
After a moment's silence, he said: "I'm clearing the school." Seconds later the plane crashed, killing all 96 on board and at least six people on the ground.

A spokesman for TAM airline could not confirm the report. "We have no information on this. We are waiting for the conclusions of the report into the accident, which should be ready in the next 90 days," the spokesman said.

Witnesses said they saw the Rio de Janeiro-bound TAM plane veer away from the school before it slammed into a number of buildings, strewing chunks of fuselage, mortar and brick throughout a three-block area.
So far 102 bodies have been found. The last one was discovered 30 hours after the accident by municipal electricians working to restore power to the area.
Only 62 of the bodies have been identified due to the badly burned state of many of the victims, said a spokesman at the city morgue.
TAM officials have declined to comment on the cause of the crash other than to say the plane lacked power.
Witnesses at the airport say they saw the thrust reverser on the Fokker's right turbine deploy automatically as the plane raced down the runway.
The thrust reverser, engaged during landings to help bring a plane to a stop, is designed to reverse the direction of the engine's thrust, creating aerodynamic resistance.

The Brazilian media speculated the TAM flight could have suffered the same fate as a Lauda-Air flight that crashed in Thailand in 1991. Investigators determined the thrust reverser on the Austrian airline's Boeing 767-300 engaged automatically, causing the plane to crash soon after takeoff.
TAM officials said such a scenario would be very unlikely.
The timing of the early morning shuttle between Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro meant a large number of the passengers were business executives.
One of the victims was drug trafficker Mauro Rodrigues Matos, whom police were waiting to arrest when the plane landed in Rio de Janeiro airport, a military police spokesman said.

Matos, who was on conditional release after serving two years of a 12-year sentence for drug dealing, was the owner of nine pounds (four kg) of cocaine found in a black plastic bag among the plane's wreckage, the spokesman said.
